messages:
maria: Quick question — do we have a proposal for splitting trace retention by feature/team rather than just env-level hot/cold? Thinking per-team retention buckets with chargeback.
aj: We talked about chargeback before. Main friction is queries: long-retention cold copies are super slow and expensive to rehydrate. Also billing model needs to be clear.
devin: Proposal: keep prod hot window 7d, extended warm 30d for critical services, and a 180d cold archive for compliance. Allow teams to pay to extend warm for specific services. :thumbsup:
elaine: Support use-case: we sometimes need 90d for debugging customer incidents. If cold takes hours to rehydrate that's not acceptable for on-call.
patrick: Two operational levers: (1) tiered retention metadata per span (env/service/feature); (2) on-demand rehydrate API with priority queue + cost tag. UX in console should show estimated restore time & cost.
maria: do we have metrics on how often support actually requests >30d traces? worth deciding policy based on data.
aj: quick numbers: last quarter ~120 rehydrate requests >30d across all prod services, avg restore size 18GB, median wait ~2.3h. Cost ~= $0.18/GB to restore from cold. So not huge volume but heavy when it happens.
patrick: We can also implement a lightweight index in warm for 90d but evict payloads to cold: keeps query latencies low for presence checks, full payload from cold on demand.
devin: Architecturally that's plausible. Index retention adds storage overhead ~10% but cuts rehydrate IO massively.
patrck (typo): sorry meant patrick — agree with index. Also recommend per-team quota on rehydrate ops to avoid noisy neighbors.
sam: Console UX: show a per-service retention toggle + a "Request extension" flow. For rehydrate, present an estimated cost and ETA before confirming. We should also include a "fast restore" paid option.
elaine: +1 for ETA and cost. On-call should be able to request emergency fast-restore with approval workflow.
infra-bot: Current trace-store: total 312TB, hot tier 18TB, warm tier 94TB, cold tier 200TB. Monthly egress for restores last 30d: 2.1TB.
aj: OTLP/exporter change: add attribute env/service and route at collector to different exporters based on retention config. Example config snippet:

```
exporters:
  s3/cold:
    bucket: traces-archive
  clickhouse/warm:
    dsn: "clickhouse://..."
processors:
  retention_router:
    rules:
      - match: {service: critical-*}
        target: warm
      - match: {env: prod}
        target: hot
```

patrick: Note: we must avoid per-request expensive evaluation in hot path. Route decisions should be tag-time or batched in collector.
maria: How do we handle rollouts? If we change routing logic, we need canary by team and fallback to current pipeline.
aj: rollout plan: feature-flagged collector code, start with 5% of traffic for a couple of low-risk services, monitor error rate & latency, then expand. Have automatic kill-switch.
devin: Also need migration tooling to sweep existing traces into new buckets for historical retention. That can be a background job with rate limits.
elaine: For compliance teams, we need an audit log of retention changes + retention-override approvals.
patrick: Security: retention metadata must be tamper-evident and we should store approvals in audit ledger.
sam: UX: console page "Trace retention" with per-service view, estimated monthly cost delta, last 90d rehydrate count, and an "apply change" modal that captures reason + approver.
maria: action items: 1) aj to draft collector routing RFC with cost model, 2) patrick to prototype warm-index design, 3) sam to mock console flow, 4) elaine to define SRE/support SLAs for restores. Meeting next Tue to review.
aj: RFC will include sample configs, rollout steps, and a backfill plan. Will ping when ready.
elaine: thanks — can we add a short query to export rehydrate history per-team? I can help with SLO numbers.
maria: yes please. I'll create RFC issue and tag everyone. Thanks all :rocket:
